sections.content: You know *aunque* and *sin embargo* from A2 Unit 28. This lesson adds *a pesar de* + noun or infinitive, *a pesar de que* + a full clause, and *pese a*, to concede a difficulty and go on.

items.spanish: A pesar de las dificultades, continuamos.
A pesar de que era caro, decidimos comprarlo.
items.english: Although it was expensive, we decided to buy it.

items.spanish: A pesar de ser caro, el proyecto puede traer buenos resultados.
items.english: Despite being expensive, the project can bring good results.

sections.content: *A pesar de* is followed by a noun or an infinitive (*a pesar de ser caro*); before a full clause use *a pesar de que* (*a pesar de que era caro*), with the indicative when the fact is real. *Pese a* means the same: *pese a las dificultades*.
